name: Éamon de Valera
role: Irish revolutionary leader; head of government (1932-48, 1951-54, 1957-59) and President of Ireland (1959-73)
summary: De Valera led Fianna Fáil, dismantled the Treaty ties to Britain in the 1930s, wrote the 1937 Constitution with its Catholic and family provisions, and kept Ireland neutral in the Second World War while using emergency law against the IRA. He backed tariff protection and Irish-controlled industry, and made ending partition the aim of his later foreign policy.
